title: Table shuffleboard: slide the weight down a 9-ft board with one push so it stops in the 3-point zone
instruction: Slide the red-capped weight down the shuffleboard with one push so that it stops in the 3-point zone at the far end: completely past the 3-line, 6 inches from the end, without falling off. Keep it on the board: slide it, do not throw it, and do not touch it again once it has left your hand.
context: Table shuffleboard is a fixture of bars, clubs and game rooms; the 9-ft size is sold for apartments and small bars. On a waxed board the weight's travel grows with the square of its speed, so stopping in a 6-inch zone 2 m away needs one clean release at the right speed, flat and straight, with no chance to correct it.
setup: A 9-ft table shuffleboard playfield built from a Hampton Bay 8 ft x 25 in x 1.5 in unfinished birch butcher-block countertop ($274 at Home Depot), cut to 7 ft 8 in x 20 in (2.337 x 0.508 m), sealed with polyurethane and dusted with silicone shuffleboard wax. Its top is 30 in (0.762 m) above the floor on a stand (two sawhorses will do; the simulation draws a table frame), running straight ahead of the robot from x = 0.280 m to 2.617 m, centred on y = -0.305 m; its near end is 205 mm in front of the robot's pedestals, with the near end gutter between them. Gutters 65 mm below the board, 100 mm wide along the sides and 200 mm long at each end (drawn as a wooden cradle; any tray or padded catch will do, as a weight that falls off scores 0 either way). Lines 6 mm wide (tape or paint): one foul line across the middle (1.448 m), and at each end the 3-line 6 in and the 2-line 12 in from the end (far end: 2.465 m and 2.312 m). One regulation weight (as in McClure's 2 5/16 in weights with plastic caps): a chrome-plated steel puck 2 5/16 in (58.7 mm) across and 0.75 in high with a red plastic cap 55 mm across and 13 mm high, 345 g in all, on the board's centre line at x = 0.315 m, 35 mm from the near end. Two YAM arms on 750 mm pedestals at x = 0, y = +/-0.305 m (the right arm straight behind the weight), 40 N parallel grippers.
scoring: The trial scores 0 if the weight is ever more than 5 mm above the board with nothing touching it (thrown), if the robot touches it after it has left the hand sliding at 0.1 m/s or more, if it leaves the board after the shot (into a gutter), or if the table moves. Otherwise the score is set by where the weight comes to rest after the shot, flat (under 10 degrees), untouched and still (under 5 mm/s for 1 s); as in the game, a weight touching a line counts the lower zone: 1.0 completely past the 3-line (6 in from the far end), including a weight hanging over the end; 0.5 completely past the 2-line (12 in from the end); 0.25 completely past the foul line in the middle; 0 short of it.
reset_notes: Before the session, slip thin nitrile finger cots over the gripper pads so no wax reaches the shared rig; remove them after. Between trials, stand the weight back on the centre line 35 mm from the near end and brush the playfield smooth. Before each set of trials, push a weight down the board by hand and film it at 60 fps beside a tape measure: it must slow by 0.18 to 0.22 m/s each second (friction 0.02). Sprinkle on silicone shuffleboard wax to make the board faster, or wipe some off to make it slower, and check again.
fidelity: PhysX at 960 Hz, 20 Hz control. Sizes and mass from tournament rules and makers' specifications; the playfield has a 9-ft table's size. The waxed board is a uniform friction of 0.02 (a fast board; published examples range from 0.012 to 0.08), not loose silicone beads; the board is perfectly flat, the puck a straight cylinder without its slight taper, no air drag, plain wooden gutters. Unmodified YAM arms, 40 N grippers.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (600 steps; never touched the weight); demo: 1.0 (scripted; released at 0.92 m/s, at rest 65 mm past the 3-line)
